54956 because three members of the City Council may be participating in the joint meeting as members of the
EAC and GPAC.

MINUTES
  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  WITH THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND CITY COUNCIL
  TUESDAY, DECEMBER 15, 2020

  A Special Joint Meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee (EAC) with the General Plan
  Advisory Committee (GPAC), and City Council was called to order by Mayor Zuckerman at 6:00
  p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this meeting was held via
  teleconference.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  City Council Members Present:  Zuckerman, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura

  City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan

  EAC Members Present:  Chan-Southwell, Bacinski, Radocchio, Schachter, Uppal,
  Yoo

  EAC Members Absent:  Bain, Larson

  GPAC Members Present:  Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Carman, Carrese, Corman,
  Friedman, Shinn

  GPAC Members Absent:  Buresh, Medawar, Seamans, Silvano

  Staff Members Present:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Community Development/Public Works
  Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Jonathan Cain, Sapphos Environmental Inc.
  Laura Male, Sapphos Environmental Inc.
  Ryan Johnson, Alta
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International
  Seth Contreras, Fehr & Peers

  3.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE

  4.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  SUSTAINABILITY ELEMENT

  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager introduced the consultants from Sapphos Environmental Inc.
  to provide the presentation on the Sustainability Element.

  Jonathan Cain, Sapphos Environmental Inc. stated that this first meeting will be on the visioning
  behind the Sustainability Element.

  Mr. Cain asked the committee to provide their definition of sustainability.

  Responses included:

  -  Forwarding a healthy environment for future generations both in nature and resources.
  -  To reduce environmental impacts as much as is practical.
  -  Preserving the environment and natural resources for future generations
  -  Maintain healthy air quality and recycling efficiency.
  -  Meeting of environment, community and economy aligning built environment with present
  and future needs.
  -  Caring for the environment for the sake of future generations.
  -  Reducing and re-using resources
SPECIAL JOINT MEETING MINUTES,
  1
DECEMBER 15, 2020
   -  Living a life that respects our resources.
  -  Reduce environmental impacts as much as is practical.
  -  Establishing city policies that sustain or improve our environment for the betterment of our
  community and region.

  Mr. Cain provided the overall vision of the sustainability element as laid out in the scope for the
  project:

  Engage the community in establishing a blueprint for steady, responsible action in addressing the
  effects of climate change, so we leave a cleaner, more stable environment for future generations.

  Mayor Zuckerman commented that is shouldn’t be limited to the effects of climate change, since
  there are other environmental issues in the City.

  Committee Member Corman agreed that it should be a broader definition.

  Committee Member Bayer stated that the air quality is also an issue in the City.

  Mayor Zuckerman stated that another specific item to consider is storm water capture and
  treatment.

  Mr. Cain provided the goal of the sustainability element per the scope of the project is as follows:

  Focus on sustainability and a low-carbon future.

  Mr. Cain stated that the sustainability components are intended to be integrated throughout the
  General Plan, most importantly in land use and transportation.

  Mr. Cain stated that the project is being funded by a planning grant through the Southern California
  Association of Governments (SCAG) and will be designed for consistency with the Regional
  Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy; the City’s Climate Action Plan; and,
  General Plan Updates.

  Mr. Cain provided a list of topics that came from the stakeholder outreach interviews in 2017.

  Mayor Zuckerman pointed out that traffic was also a most often referred to topic.

  Mr. Cain provided a list of community, regional and local stakeholders, who they will conduct
  outreach with, on the Sustainability Element.

  Additions to the lists recommended by the Council and Committee Members include:

  -  Non-profits and other community groups
  -  Rolling Hills Country Club
  -  Water Board
  -  Sanitation Department
  -  Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy
  -  Los Angeles County West Vector Control
  -  Homeowners Associations

  Ryan Johnson, Transportation Planner, Alta, provided an overview on outreach and engagement
  strategies.

  Mayor Zuckerman stated that the equestrian community has a newsletter that is published on a
  regular basis.

  Committee Member Bacinski stated that Dapplegray Lanes has a monthly newsletter.

  Mr. Johnson provided an overview of the Interactive Web Map, which will be available on the
  General Plan Update page of the City’s website.

  Council Member Stegura inquired about how to drive traffic to the website. Mr. Johnson stated
  that the City’s existing social media accounts will be used, as well as posting on the General Plan
  Update page and the City’s overall web page, posting flyers at community and/or private locations,
  and possibly posting at trails and available message boards.
SPECIAL JOINT MEETING MINUTES,
  2
DECEMBER 15, 2020
   Council Member Stegura suggested providing information to the Homeowners Association.
  Committee Member Bayer added that the Homeowners Associations have websites that are a great
  source to disseminate information.

  In response to a question by Mayor Zuckerman, Mr. Johnson stated that there is a video tutorial
  on how to use the Interactive Web Map. In addition, he will look into a YouTube demonstration
  on how to use the site.

  Council Member Schmitz concurred with Mayor Zuckerman’s comments and would like to ensure
  that there are alternative ways of providing input.

  Mr. Cain provided an overview of the content and sections included in the Sustainability Element.
  Seven pillars have been defined as the framework to focus and organize analysis and goal setting,
  they include:

  1.  Air Quality
  2.  Waste Management & Recycling
  3.  Water Resources
  4.  Energy
  5.  Mobility
  6.  Land Use
  7.  Quality of Life

  Mr. Cain stated that after this meeting, a survey will be sent to the committee to list goals for each
  of these seven pillars and metrics for each goal.

  Committee Member Bacinski commented that there are pools throughout the City that are not
  being used and they waste resources; could encouraging homeowners to fill in their pools be
  included as a goal. Mr. Cain stated that this could be included as a goal and should be a measurable
  goal.

  Council Member Schmitz commented that, regionally or throughout the State, there are policies
  on gray water usage. Mr. Cain stated that as a goal, this could be increased use of gray water, how
  it will be used, and how the success of a gray water program could be measured.

  Per a request by Mayor Zuckerman, Mr. Cain stated that committee members will be provided
  with examples of Sustainability Elements in existing General Plans.

  The committee discussed and provided a preliminary list of goals for each of the seven pillars.

  Water Resources
  Goals: Current conservation of potable water
  Reducing runoff
  Gray water education program for private residents
  Gray water usage for commercial properties
  Water quality
  Runoff from irrigation systems
  Creating or enabling a system to take advantage of water efficiency rebate programs
  Rain barrel program

  Energy
  Goals: Reduction of fossil fuels
  Reduction of airborne carbon
  Education on energy efficiency programs
  Reevaluate building codes to require energy efficiency

  Air Quality
  Goals: Reliable measures of the city’s current air quality

  Waste and Recycling
  Goals: Composting
  Education on composting
  Reduction of plastic bottles
  Waste to energy (horse manure)
SPECIAL JOINT MEETING MINUTES,
  3
DECEMBER 15, 2020
   Mobility
  Goals: Improving mobility in the commercial district
  Ways to reduce the heat island effect
  Maintain existing trails and walkways
  Mid-block crosswalks in the commercial district

  Land Use
  Goals: Increasing/connecting green zones with the commercial district
  Providing a reasonable degree of goods and services in the business district
  Reduce traffic

  Quality of Life
  Goals: Noise abatement programs
  Preserve the cultural character of the community

  5.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  6.  ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Zuckerman adjourned the meeting at 8:00 p.m.
